columns.name: description

columns.name: syntax
columns.comment: How the combinator is applied to an aggregate function name.

columns.name: examples
columns.comment: Usage examples.

columns.name: introduced_in

name: asynchronous_inserts
comment: Contains information about pending asynchronous inserts in queue in server's memory.

columns.name: query
columns.comment: Query text.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: format
columns.comment: Format name.

columns.name: first_update
columns.comment: First insert time with microseconds resolution.

columns.name: total_bytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes waiting in the queue.

columns.name: entries.query_id
columns.comment: Array of query ids of the inserts waiting in the queue.

columns.name: entries.bytes
columns.comment: Array of bytes of each insert query waiting in the queue.

name: asynchronous_loader
comment: Contains information and status for recent asynchronous jobs (e.g. for tables loading). The table contains a row for every job.

columns.name: job
columns.comment: Job name (may be not unique).

columns.name: job_id
columns.comment: Unique ID of the job.

columns.name: dependencies
columns.comment: List of IDs of jobs that should be done before this job.

columns.name: dependencies_left
columns.comment: Current number of dependencies left to be done.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Current load status of a job: PENDING: Load job is not started yet. OK: Load job executed and was successful. FAILED: Load job executed and failed. CANCELED: Load job is not going to be executed due to removal or dependency failure.

columns.name: is_executing
columns.comment: The job is currently being executed by a worker.

columns.name: is_blocked
columns.comment: The job waits for its dependencies to be done.

columns.name: is_ready
columns.comment: The job is ready to be executed and waits for a worker.

columns.name: elapsed
columns.comment: Seconds elapsed since start of execution. Zero if job is not started. Total execution time if job finished.

columns.name: pool_id
columns.comment: ID of a pool currently assigned to the job.

columns.name: pool
columns.comment: Name of `pool_id` pool.

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Priority of `pool_id` pool.

columns.name: execution_pool_id
columns.comment: ID of a pool the job is executed in. Equals initially assigned pool before execution starts.

columns.name: execution_pool
columns.comment: Name of `execution_pool_id` pool.

columns.name: execution_priority
columns.comment: Priority of execution_pool_id pool.

columns.name: ready_seqno
columns.comment: Not null for ready jobs. Worker pulls the next job to be executed from a ready queue of its pool. If there are multiple ready jobs, then job with the lowest value of `ready_seqno` is picked.

columns.name: waiters
columns.comment: The number of threads waiting on this job.

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Not null for failed and canceled jobs. Holds error message raised during query execution or error leading to cancelling of this job along with dependency failure chain of job names.

columns.name: schedule_time
columns.comment: Time when job was created and scheduled to be executed (usually with all its dependencies).

columns.name: enqueue_time
columns.comment: Time when job became ready and was enqueued into a ready queue of it's pool. Null if the job is not ready yet.

columns.name: start_time
columns.comment: Time when worker dequeues the job from ready queue and start its execution. Null if the job is not started yet.

columns.name: finish_time
columns.comment: Time when job execution is finished. Null if the job is not finished yet.

name: asynchronous_metric_log
comment: Contains the historical values for system.asynchronous_metrics, once per time interval (one second by default).

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Event date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

columns.name: metric
columns.comment: Metric name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Metric value.

name: asynchronous_metrics
comment: Contains metrics that are calculated periodically in the background. For example, the amount of RAM in use.

columns.name: metric
columns.comment: Metric name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Metric value.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: Metric description.

name: azure_queue_metadata_cache
comment: Contains in-memory state of AzureQueue metadata and currently processed rows per file.

columns.name: zookeeper_path
columns.comment: Path in zookeeper to metadata

columns.name: file_path
columns.comment: File path of a file which is being processed

columns.name: file_name
columns.comment: File name of a file which is being processed

columns.name: rows_processed
columns.comment: Currently processed number of rows

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Status of processing: Processed, Processing, Failed

columns.name: processing_start_time
columns.comment: Time at which processing of the file started

columns.name: processing_end_time
columns.comment: Time at which processing of the file ended

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Exception which happened during processing

name: azure_queue_settings
comment: Contains a list of settings of AzureQueue tables.

columns.name: database

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table with AzureQueue engine.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Setting name.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Setting value.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Setting type (implementation specific string value).

columns.name: changed

columns.name: description
columns.comment: Setting description.

columns.name: alterable
columns.comment: Shows whether the current user can change the setting via ALTER TABLE MODIFY SETTING: 0 — Current user can't change the setting, 1 — Current user can change the setting.

name: background_schedule_pool
comment: Contains information about tasks in all BackgroundSchedulePool instances. Each row represents a task.

columns.name: pool
columns.comment: Pool name. Possible values: `schedule` (general purpose schedule pool), `buffer_flush` (pool for flushing Buffer table data), `distributed` (pool for distributed table operations), `message_broker` (pool for message broker operations), `streaming` (pool for streaming queries background jobs), `iceberg` (pool for Iceberg table metadata refresh).

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: table_uuid
columns.comment: Table UUID.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query ID (if executing now). Note: this is not a real query, but a randomly generated ID for matching logs in `system.text_log`.

columns.name: elapsed_ms
columns.comment: Task execution time (if executing now).

columns.name: log_name
columns.comment: Log name for the task.

columns.name: deactivated
columns.comment: Whether the task is deactivated (always false, since deactivated tasks are removed from the pool).

columns.name: scheduled
columns.comment: Whether the task is scheduled for execution.

columns.name: delayed
columns.comment: Whether the task is scheduled with delay.

columns.name: executing
columns.comment: Whether the task is currently executing.

name: background_schedule_pool_log
comment: Contains history of background schedule pool task executions.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Event date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Event time with microseconds precision.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Identifier of the query associated with the background task.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: table_uuid
columns.comment: UUID of the table the background task belongs to.

columns.name: log_name
columns.comment: Name of the background task.

columns.name: duration_ms
columns.comment: Duration of the task execution in milliseconds.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: The error code of the occurred exception.

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Text message of the occurred error.

name: backups
comment: Contains a list of all BACKUP or RESTORE operations with their current states and other properties. Note, that table is not persistent and it shows only operations executed after the last server restart.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: Operation ID, can be either passed via SETTINGS id=... or be randomly generated UUID.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Operation name, a string like `Disk('backups', 'my_backup')`

columns.name: base_backup_name
columns.comment: Base Backup Operation name, a string like `Disk('backups', 'my_base_backup')`

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query ID of a query that started backup.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Status of backup or restore operation.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: The error message if any.

columns.name: start_time
columns.comment: The time when operation started.

columns.name: end_time
columns.comment: The time when operation finished.

columns.name: num_files
columns.comment: The number of files stored in the backup.

columns.name: total_size
columns.comment: The total size of files stored in the backup.

columns.name: num_entries
columns.comment: The number of entries in the backup, i.e. the number of files inside the folder if the backup is stored as a folder.

columns.name: uncompressed_size
columns.comment: The uncompressed size of the backup.

columns.name: compressed_size
columns.comment: The compressed size of the backup.

columns.name: files_read
columns.comment: Returns the number of files read during RESTORE from this backup.

columns.name: bytes_read
columns.comment: Returns the total size of files read during RESTORE from this backup.

columns.name: ProfileEvents
columns.comment: All the profile events captured during this operation.

columns.name: settings
columns.comment: Backup/restore-specific settings effectively used for this operation (from the `SETTINGS` clause, including defaults). Sensitive settings are not exposed.

columns.name: engine_settings
columns.comment: Settings effectively used by the backup engine's reader/writer (e.g. S3 `allow_native_copy`). Empty when the operation involves more than one engine that a flat map cannot represent: incremental backups and restores, lightweight snapshot restores, and non-internal `ON CLUSTER` operations.

name: build_options
comment: Contains a list of all build flags, compiler options and commit hash for used build.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the build option.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Value of the build option.

name: certificates
comment: Contains information about available certificates and their sources.

columns.name: version
columns.comment: Version of the certificate. Values are 0 for v1, 1 for v2, 2 for v3.

columns.name: serial_number
columns.comment: Serial Number of the certificate assigned by the issuer.

columns.name: signature_algo
columns.comment: Signature Algorithm - an algorithm used by the issuer to sign this certificate.

columns.name: issuer
columns.comment: Issuer - a unique identifier for the Certificate Authority issuing this certificate.

columns.name: not_before
columns.comment: The beginning of the time window when this certificate is valid.

columns.name: not_after
columns.comment: The end of the time window when this certificate is valid.

columns.name: subject
columns.comment: Subject - identifies the owner of the public key.

columns.name: pkey_algo
columns.comment: Public Key Algorithm defines the algorithm the public key can be used with.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Path to the file or directory containing this certificate.

columns.name: default
columns.comment: Certificate is in the default certificate location.

columns.name: protocol
columns.comment: Protocol name if certificate is from per-protocol TLS config, otherwise empty.

name: clusters
comment: Contains information about clusters defined in the configuration file or generated by a Replicated database.

columns.name: cluster
columns.comment: The cluster name.

columns.name: shard_num
columns.comment: The shard number in the cluster, starting from 1.

columns.name: shard_name
columns.comment: The name of the shard in the cluster.

columns.name: shard_weight
columns.comment: The relative weight of the shard when writing data.

columns.name: internal_replication
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether this host is a part on ensemble which can replicate the data on its own.

columns.name: replica_num
columns.comment: The replica number in the shard, starting from 1.

columns.name: host_name
columns.comment: The host name, as specified in the config.

columns.name: host_address
columns.comment: The host IP address obtained from DNS.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: The port to use for connecting to the server.

columns.name: is_local
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the host is local.

columns.name: user
columns.comment: The name of the user for connecting to the server.

columns.name: default_database
columns.comment: The default database name.

columns.name: errors_count
columns.comment: The number of times this host failed to reach replica.

columns.name: slowdowns_count
columns.comment: The number of slowdowns that led to changing replica when establishing a connection with hedged requests.

columns.name: estimated_recovery_time
columns.comment: Seconds remaining until the replica error count is zeroed and it is considered to be back to normal.

columns.name: database_shard_name
columns.comment: The name of the `Replicated` database shard (for clusters that belong to a `Replicated` database).

columns.name: database_replica_name
columns.comment: The name of the `Replicated` database replica (for clusters that belong to a `Replicated` database).

columns.name: is_shared_catalog_cluster
columns.comment: Bool indicating if the cluster belongs to shared catalog.

columns.name: is_active
columns.comment: The status of the Replicated database replica (for clusters that belong to a Replicated database): 1 means 'replica is online', 0 means 'replica is offline', NULL means 'unknown'.

columns.name: unsynced_after_recovery
columns.comment: Indicates if a Replicated database replica has replication lag more than max_replication_lag_to_enqueue after creating or recovering the replica.

columns.name: replication_lag
columns.comment: The replication lag of the `Replicated` database replica (for clusters that belong to a Replicated database).

columns.name: recovery_time
columns.comment: The recovery time of the `Replicated` database replica (for clusters that belong to a Replicated database), in milliseconds.

name: codecs
comment: Contains information about system codecs.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Codec name.

columns.name: method_byte
columns.comment: Byte which indicates codec in compressed file.

columns.name: is_compression
columns.comment: True if this codec compresses something. Otherwise it can be just a transformation that helps compression.

columns.name: is_generic_compression
columns.comment: The codec is a generic compression algorithm like lz4, zstd.

columns.name: is_encryption
columns.comment: The codec encrypts.

columns.name: is_timeseries_codec
columns.comment: The codec is for floating point timeseries codec.

columns.name: is_experimental
columns.comment: The codec is experimental.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: A high-level description of the codec.

name: collations
comment: Contains a list of all available collations for alphabetical comparison of strings.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the collation.

columns.name: language
columns.comment: The language.

name: columns
comment: Lists all columns from all tables of the current server.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Column name.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Column type.

columns.name: position
columns.comment: Ordinal position of a column in a table starting with 1.

columns.name: default_kind
columns.comment: Expression type (DEFAULT, MATERIALIZED, ALIAS) for the default value, or an empty string if it is not defined.

columns.name: default_expression
columns.comment: Expression for the default value, or an empty string if it is not defined.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: The size of compressed data, in bytes.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: The size of decompressed data, in bytes.

columns.name: marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of marks, in bytes.

columns.name: comment
columns.comment: Comment on the column, or an empty string if it is not defined.

columns.name: is_in_partition_key
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the column is in the partition expression.

columns.name: is_in_sorting_key
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the column is in the sorting key expression.

columns.name: is_in_primary_key
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the column is in the primary key expression.

columns.name: is_in_sampling_key
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the column is in the sampling key expression.

columns.name: compression_codec
columns.comment: Compression codec name.

columns.name: character_octet_length
columns.comment: Maximum length in bytes for binary data, character data, or text data and images. In ClickHouse makes sense only for FixedString data type. Otherwise, the NULL value is returned.

columns.name: numeric_precision
columns.comment: Accuracy of approximate numeric data, exact numeric data, integer data, or monetary data. In ClickHouse it is bit width for integer types and decimal precision for Decimal types. Otherwise, the NULL value is returned.

columns.name: numeric_precision_radix
columns.comment: The base of the number system is the accuracy of approximate numeric data, exact numeric data, integer data or monetary data. In ClickHouse it's 2 for integer types and 10 for Decimal types. Otherwise, the NULL value is returned.

columns.name: numeric_scale
columns.comment: The scale of approximate numeric data, exact numeric data, integer data, or monetary data. In ClickHouse makes sense only for Decimal types. Otherwise, the NULL value is returned.

columns.name: datetime_precision
columns.comment: Decimal precision of DateTime64 data type. For other data types, the NULL value is returned.

columns.name: serialization_hint
columns.comment: A hint for column to choose serialization on inserts according to statistics.

columns.name: statistics
columns.comment: The types of statistics created in this columns.

name: completions
comment: Contains a list of completion tokens.

columns.name: word
columns.comment: Completion token.

columns.name: context
columns.comment: Token entity kind (e.g. table).

columns.name: belongs
columns.comment: Token for entity, this token belongs to (e.g. name of owning database).

name: constraints

columns.name: database

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: name

columns.name: type

columns.name: expression

name: contributors

name: current_roles

columns.name: role_name

columns.name: with_admin_option
columns.comment: 1 if the role has ADMIN OPTION privilege.

columns.name: is_default
columns.comment: 1 if role is set to be a default.

columns.name: title

columns.name: granularity

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: The size of compressed data, in bytes.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: The size of decompressed data, in bytes.

columns.name: marks_bytes

columns.name: is_readonly

columns.name: max_log_ptr

columns.name: replica_name

columns.comment: Path to replica data in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: metadata_path
columns.comment: Metadata path.

columns.name: uuid

columns.name: engine_full

columns.name: comment
columns.comment: Database comment.

columns.name: is_external

columns.name: table
columns.comment: The name of the table this part belongs to.

columns.name: partition_id
columns.comment: The identifier of the partition this part belongs to.

columns.name: name

name: dictionaries

columns.comment: Name of the database containing the dictionary created by DDL query. Empty string for other dictionaries.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Dictionary name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Dictionary UUID.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Dictionary status. Possible values: NOT_LOADED — Dictionary not currently loaded in memory, LOADED — Dictionary loaded successfully, FAILED — Unable to load the dictionary as a result of an error, LOADING — Dictionary is loading now, LOADED_AND_RELOADING — Dictionary is loaded successfully, and is being reloaded right now (frequent reasons: SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARY query, timeout, dictionary co…

columns.name: origin
columns.comment: Path to the configuration file that describes the dictionary.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Type of a dictionary allocation. Storing Dictionaries in Memory.

columns.name: key.names
columns.comment: Array of key names provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: key.types
columns.comment: Corresponding array of key types provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: attribute.names
columns.comment: Array of attribute names provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: attribute.types
columns.comment: Corresponding array of attribute types provided by the dictionary.

columns.name: bytes_allocated
columns.comment: Amount of RAM allocated for the dictionary.

columns.name: hierarchical_index_bytes_allocated
columns.comment: Amount of RAM allocated for hierarchical index.

columns.name: query_count

columns.name: hit_rate
columns.comment: For cache dictionaries, the percentage of uses for which the value was in the cache.

columns.name: found_rate

columns.name: element_count
columns.comment: Number of items stored in the dictionary.

columns.name: load_factor
columns.comment: Percentage filled in the dictionary (for a hashed dictionary, the percentage filled in the hash table).

columns.name: source
columns.comment: Text describing the data source for the dictionary.

columns.name: lifetime_min

columns.name: related

columns.name: related

name: disks

columns.name: name

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Path to the mount point in the file system.

columns.comment: Free space on disk in bytes.

columns.name: total_space

columns.comment: Free space which is not taken by reservations (free_space minus the size of reservations taken by merges, inserts, and other disk write operations currently running).

columns.name: keep_free_space
columns.comment: Amount of disk space that should stay free on disk in bytes. Defined in the keep_free_space_bytes parameter of disk configuration.

columns.name: type

columns.name: object_storage_type

columns.name: metadata_type

columns.name: is_encrypted

columns.name: is_read_only
columns.comment: Flag which indicates that you can only perform read operations with this disk.

columns.name: is_remote
columns.comment: Flag which indicated what operations with this disk involve network interaction.

columns.name: is_broken
columns.comment: Flag which indicates if disk is broken. Broken disks will have 0 space and cannot be used.

columns.name: cache_path

columns.name: last_exception

columns.name: ip_family
columns.comment: IP address family.

columns.name: cached_at
columns.comment: Record cached timestamp.

name: documentation
comment: Collects the embedded documentation of the components of the system (functions, table engines, data types, settings, profile events, metrics, system tables, etc.) into a single table, with the reference documentation rendered as Markdown and the path to the source file where it is defined.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the entity, e.g. `domainWithoutWWW` or `MergeTree`.

columns.name: type
columns.type: Enum8('Function' = 1, 'Aggregate Function' = 2, 'Table Function' = 3, 'Table Engine' = 4, 'Database Engine' = 5, 'Data Type' = 6, 'Dictionary Layout' = 7, 'Dictionary Source' = 8, 'Aggregate Function Combinator' = 9, 'Data Skipping Index' = 10, 'Disk Type' = 11, 'Setting' = 12, 'MergeTree Setting' = 13, 'Server Setting' = 14, 'Format' = 15, 'Compression Codec' = 16, 'Profile Event' = 17, 'Current Metric' = 18, 'Asynchronous Metric' = 19, 'System Table' = 20)
columns.comment: The kind of the entity, e.g. `Function` or `Table Engine`.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: The reference documentation of the entity rendered as Markdown, assembled from the embedded documentation (the same content as published on the website), including syntax, examples and other structured parts, if any.

columns.name: source
columns.comment: The path to the source file where the entity's documentation is defined, relative to the repository root. Empty if the source location is unknown.

name: dropped_tables
comment: Contains a list of tables which were dropped from Atomic databases but not completely removed yet.

columns.name: index
columns.comment: Index in marked_dropped_tables queue.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table UUID.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Table engine name.

columns.name: metadata_dropped_path
columns.comment: Path of table's metadata file in metadata_dropped directory.

columns.name: table_dropped_time
columns.comment: The time when the next attempt to remove table's data is scheduled on. Usually it's the table when the table was dropped plus `database_atomic_delay_before_drop_table_sec`.

name: dropped_tables_parts
comment: Contains parts of system.dropped_tables tables

columns.name: partition
columns.comment: Partition identifier (string representation derived from the table partition key expression).

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the data part. The part naming structure can be used to determine many aspects of the data, ingest, and merge patterns. The part naming format is the following:

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: The UUID of data part.

columns.name: part_type
columns.comment: The data part storing format. Possible values: `Wide` — each column is stored in a separate file, `Compact` — all columns are stored in one file. Data storing format is controlled by the `min_bytes_for_wide_part` and `min_rows_for_wide_part` settings of the MergeTree table.

columns.name: active
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the data part is active. If a data part is active, it's used in a table. Otherwise, it's about to be deleted. Inactive data parts appear after merging and mutating operations.

columns.name: marks
columns.comment: The number of marks. To get the approximate number of rows in a data part, multiply marks by the index granularity (usually 8192) (this hint does not work for adaptive granularity).

columns.name: rows
columns.comment: The number of rows.

columns.name: files
columns.comment: The number of files in the data part.

columns.name: bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the data part files in bytes.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: primary_key_size
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values in the primary.idx/cidx file on disk.

columns.name: marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks.

columns.name: secondary_indices_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data for secondary indices in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: secondary_indices_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data for secondary indices in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: secondary_indices_marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks for secondary indices.

columns.name: modification_time
columns.comment: The time the directory with the data part was modified. This usually corresponds to the time of data part creation.

columns.name: remove_time
columns.comment: The time when the data part became inactive.

columns.name: refcount
columns.comment: The number of places where the data part is used. A value greater than 2 indicates that the data part is used in queries or merges.

columns.name: min_date
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: max_date
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: min_time
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: max_time
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: partition_id
columns.comment: ID of the partition.

columns.name: min_block_number
columns.comment: The minimum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: max_block_number
columns.comment: The maximum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: level
columns.comment: Depth of the merge tree. Zero means that the current part was created by insert rather than by merging other parts.

columns.name: data_version
columns.comment: Number that is used to determine which mutations should be applied to the data part (mutations with a version higher than data_version).

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values. Will be 0 when `primary_key_lazy_load` is enabled and the key is not loaded. When non-zero the bytes live in the part itself and are accounted within `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`. They are NEVER counted in `PrimaryIndexCacheBytes` — those are mutually exclusive per part: an index lives either in the part (this metric) or in …

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for primary key values. Will be 0 when `primary_key_lazy_load` is enabled and the key is not loaded. When non-zero, included in `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`. See the note on `primary_key_bytes_in_memory` for the relationship with `PrimaryIndexCacheBytes`.

columns.name: index_granularity_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by index granularity values (will be 0 in case of primary_key_lazy_load=1 and use_primary_key_cache=1). When non-zero the bytes are part-owned and accounted within `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`.

columns.name: index_granularity_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for index granularity values (will be 0 in case of primary_key_lazy_load=1 and use_primary_key_cache=1). When non-zero, included in `jemalloc.mergetree_arena.active_bytes`.

columns.name: is_frozen
columns.comment: Flag that shows that a partition data backup exists. 1, the backup exists. 0, the backup does not exist. For more details, see FREEZE PARTITION.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Name of the table engine without parameters.

columns.name: disk_name
columns.comment: Name of a disk that stores the data part.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Absolute path to the folder with data part files.

columns.name: hash_of_all_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of compressed files.

columns.name: hash_of_uncompressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of uncompressed files (files with marks, index file etc.).

columns.name: uncompressed_hash_of_compressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of data in the compressed files as if they were uncompressed.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_max

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.expression

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: projections
columns.comment: The list of projection names calculated for this part.

columns.name: visible
columns.comment: Flag which indicated whether this part is visible for SELECT queries.

columns.name: removal_tid_lock

columns.name: removal_tid

columns.name: removal_csn

columns.name: has_lightweight_delete
columns.comment: The flag which indicated whether the part has lightweight delete mask.

columns.name: last_removal_attempt_time
columns.comment: The last time the server tried to delete this part.

columns.name: removal_state
columns.comment: The current state of part removal process.

name: enabled_roles

columns.name: is_default

name: error_log

columns.name: hostname

columns.name: event_date

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

name: errors

columns.name: value

columns.name: last_error_time
columns.comment: The time when the last error happened.

columns.name: last_error_message

columns.name: last_error_format_string
columns.comment: Format string for the last error.

columns.name: last_error_trace
columns.comment: A stack trace that represents a list of physical addresses where the called methods are stored.

columns.name: remote

name: filesystem_cache
comment: Contains information about all entries inside filesystem cache for remote objects.

columns.name: cache_base_path

columns.name: file_segment_range_end

columns.name: size

columns.name: state

columns.name: finished_download_time

columns.name: cache_hits

columns.name: references

columns.name: downloaded_size
columns.comment: Downloaded size of the file segment

columns.name: kind

columns.name: unbound

columns.name: user_id

columns.name: segment_type

columns.name: file_size

name: filesystem_cache_settings
comment: Contains information about all filesystem cache settings

columns.name: cache_name
columns.comment: Cache name

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Cache directory path

columns.name: max_size
columns.comment: Maximum cache size

columns.name: max_elements
columns.comment: Maximum number of cache elements, e.g. file segments (limits number of files on filesystem)

columns.name: max_file_segment_size
columns.comment: Maximum size of a single file segment

columns.name: boundary_alignment
columns.comment: File segment alignment

columns.name: reserve_granularity
columns.comment: When reserving space for a file segment download, reserve at least this many bytes ahead of the downloaded size (capped at the file segment size). Coarser granularity reduces the rate of cache state lock acquisitions on the reservation hot path, at the cost of holding some reserved-but-not-yet-downloaded space (reclaimed on file segment completion). Value 0 disables reserve-ahead: space is rese…

columns.name: cache_on_write_operations
columns.comment: Enables write-through cache (cache on INSERT and MERGE)

columns.name: cache_policy
columns.comment: Cache eviction policy

columns.name: slru_size_ratio
columns.comment: SLRU cache policy size ratio of protected to probationary elements

columns.name: background_download_threads
columns.comment: Number of background download threads. Value 0 disables background download

columns.name: background_download_queue_size_limit
columns.comment: Size of background download queue. Value 0 disables background download

columns.name: background_download_max_file_segment_size
columns.comment: Maximum size which can be downloaded in background download

columns.name: load_metadata_threads
columns.comment: Maximum number of threads used to load cache metadata at server startup

columns.name: load_metadata_asynchronously
columns.comment: Enables asynchronous loading of metadata on server startup

columns.name: keep_free_space_size_ratio
columns.comment: A ratio of free space which cache would try to uphold in the background

columns.name: keep_free_space_elements_ratio
columns.comment: A ratio of free elements which cache would try to uphold in the background

columns.name: keep_free_space_remove_batch
columns.comment: A remove batch size of cache elements made by background thread which upholds free space/elements ratio

columns.name: keep_free_space_eviction_threads
columns.comment: Number of threads which perform the actual file segment removal (filesystem deletion) for the background free space/elements ratio keeping. The single background thread collects eviction candidates and frees their priority queue entries, while these threads do the lock-free removal in parallel

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_interval_ms
columns.comment: Idle interval in milliseconds of the background task which purges invalidated (lazily-removed) priority queue entries

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_threshold
columns.comment: Number of accumulated invalidated priority queue entries which triggers their background removal

columns.name: invalidated_entries_cleanup_remove_batch
columns.comment: Maximum number of invalidated priority queue entries removed under a single write lock per background iteration

columns.name: enable_filesystem_query_cache_limit
columns.comment: Enable limiting maximum size of cache which can be written within a query

columns.name: cache_hits_threshold
columns.comment: Deprecated setting

columns.name: enable_bypass_cache_with_threshold
columns.comment: Undocumented. Not recommended for use

columns.name: bypass_cache_threshold
columns.comment: Undocumented. Not recommended for use

columns.name: write_cache_per_user_id_directory
columns.comment: Internal ClickHouse Cloud setting

columns.name: allow_dynamic_cache_resize
columns.comment: Allow dynamic resize of filesystem cache

columns.name: dynamic_resize_lock_wait_ms
columns.comment: Timeout in milliseconds to acquire the dynamic resize exclusive lock before skipping the resize attempt

columns.name: max_size_ratio_to_total_space
columns.comment: Ratio of `max_size` to total disk space

columns.name: skip_cache_on_disk_failure
columns.comment: If true, bypass filesystem cache operations silently on disk IO errors. If false (default), disk IO errors are propagated as startup failures.

columns.name: use_split_cache
columns.comment: Use separation of files to system/data.

columns.name: split_cache_ratio
columns.comment: Ratio of system segment to total size of cache for split_cache.

columns.name: overcommit_eviction_evict_step
columns.comment: Eviction step in bytes for overcommit eviction policy. Used for keep_free_space_*_ratio settings

columns.name: check_cache_probability
columns.comment: Works only for debug or sanitizer build. Checks cache correctness by going through all cache and checking state of each cache element

columns.name: idle_client_ttl_sec

columns.comment: 1 if this process is a part mutation.

columns.name: total_size_bytes_compressed
columns.comment: The total size of the compressed data in the merged chunks.

columns.name: total_size_bytes_uncompressed
columns.comment: The total size of compressed data in the merged chunks.

columns.name: total_size_marks
columns.comment: The total number of marks in the merged parts.

columns.name: bytes_read_uncompressed
columns.comment: Number of bytes read, uncompressed.

columns.name: rows_read
columns.comment: Number of rows read.

columns.name: bytes_written_uncompressed
columns.comment: Number of bytes written, uncompressed.

columns.name: rows_written
columns.comment: Number of rows written.

columns.name: columns_written
columns.comment: Number of columns written (for Vertical merge algorithm).

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Memory consumption of the merge process.

columns.name: thread_id
columns.comment: Thread ID of the merge process.

columns.name: merge_type
columns.comment: The type of current merge. Empty if it's an mutation.

columns.name: merge_algorithm
columns.comment: The algorithm used in current merge. Empty if it's an mutation.

columns.name: current_projection
columns.comment: The name of the projection currently being merged or rebuilt. Empty if not in the projection merge stage.

columns.name: current_projection_progress
columns.comment: The progress of the current projection merge from 0 to 1.

columns.name: current_projection_parts_merging
columns.comment: The number of projection parts currently being merged.

columns.name: current_projection_parts_remaining
columns.comment: The number of projection parts remaining to be merged for the current projection.

columns.name: projections_completed
columns.comment: The list of projections that have been merged or rebuilt so far.

columns.name: projections_remaining
columns.comment: The list of projections that still need to be merged or rebuilt.

name: metric_log
comment: Contains history of metrics values from tables system.metrics and system.events, periodically flushed to disk.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Event date.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Event time.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Event time with microseconds resolution.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_Query
columns.comment: Number of queries to be interpreted and potentially executed. Does not include queries that failed to parse or were rejected due to AST size limits, quota limits or limits on the number of simultaneously running queries. May include internal queries initiated by ClickHouse itself. Does not count subqueries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InitialQuery
columns.comment: Same as Query, but only counts initial queries (see is_initial_query).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InitialSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as InitialQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count SELECT queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQueriesWithSubqueries
columns.comment: Count INSERT queries with all subqueries

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueriesWithPrimaryKeyUsage
columns.comment: Count SELECT queries which use the primary key to evaluate the WHERE condition

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as InsertQuery, but only for asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertBytes
columns.comment: Data size in bytes of asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertRows
columns.comment: Number of rows inserted by asynchronous INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AsyncInsertCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a duplicate hash id has been found in asynchronous INSERT hash id cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed internal queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInternalQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInternalInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInternalQuery, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInitialQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed initial queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInitialSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedInitialQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedQuery
columns.comment: Number of total failed queries, both internal and user queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedSelectQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedInsertQuery
columns.comment: Same as FailedQuery, but only for INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FailedAsyncInsertQuery
columns.comment: Number of failed ASYNC INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerQueries
columns.comment: Number of fuzzed queries attempted by the server-side AST fuzzer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedBackupRestore
columns.comment: Number of fuzzed BACKUP/RESTORE queries the server-side AST fuzzer skipped instead of executing.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ASTFuzzerSkippedReplicatedDDLInternal
columns.comment: Number of times the server-side AST fuzzer skipped fuzzing because an internal replicated-database DDL execution (a live ZooKeeperMetadataTransaction) was in flight on the context.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of all queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_SelectQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of SELECT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_InsertQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of INSERT queries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OtherQueryTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time of queries that are not SELECT or INSERT.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileOpen
columns.comment: Number of files opened.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_Seek
columns.comment: Number of times the 'lseek' function was called.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorRead
columns.comment: Number of reads (read/pread) from a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadFailed
columns.comment: Number of times the read (read/pread) from a file descriptor have failed.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show the compressed data size.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWrite
columns.comment: Number of writes (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteFailed
columns.comment: Number of times the write (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor have failed.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written to file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show compressed data size.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileSync
columns.comment: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DirectorySync
columns.comment: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for directories.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FileSyncElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for files.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DirectorySyncElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for directories.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReadCompressedBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes (the number of bytes before decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferBlocks
columns.comment: Number of compressed blocks (the blocks of data that are compressed independent of each other) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferBytes
columns.comment: Number of uncompressed bytes (the number of bytes after decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatch
columns.comment: Number of times the compressed block checksum did not match.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatchSingleBitMismatch
columns.comment: Number of times a compressed block checksum mismatch was caused by a single-bit difference.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CompressedReadBufferChecksumDoesntMatchMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent detecting bit-flips due to compressed block checksum mismatches.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has been found in the uncompressed cache (and decompression was avoided).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has not been found in the uncompressed cache (and required decompression).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UncompressedCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Number of bytes evicted from the uncompressed cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has been found in the userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a block of data has not been found in the userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Number of bytes evicted from the userspace page cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheResized
columns.comment: Number of times the userspace page cache was auto-resized (typically happens a few times per second, controlled by memory_worker_period_ms).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheOvercommitResize
columns.comment: Number of times the userspace page cache was auto-resized to free memory during a memory allocation.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PageCacheReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read from userspace page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MMappedFileCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we didn't have to mmap it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MMappedFileCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a file has not been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we had to mmap it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we didn't have to open it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we had to open it again.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_OpenedFileCacheMicroseconds
columns.comment: Amount of time spent executing OpenedFileCache methods.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOWrite
columns.comment: Number of writes with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOWriteBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIORead
columns.comment: Number of reads with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AIOReadBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IOBufferAllocs
columns.comment: Number of allocations of IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IOBufferAllocBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes allocated for IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ArenaAllocChunks
columns.comment: Number of chunks allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ArenaAllocBytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FunctionExecute
columns.comment: Number of SQL ordinary function calls (SQL functions are called on per-block basis, so this number represents the number of blocks).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TableFunctionExecute
columns.comment: Number of table function calls.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DefaultImplementationForNullsRows
columns.comment: Number of rows processed by default implementation for nulls in function execution

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DefaultImplementationForNullsRowsWithNulls
columns.comment: Number of rows which contain null values processed by default implementation for nulls in function execution

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MarkCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the mark cache, so we didn't have to load a mark file.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_MarkCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the mark cache, so we had to load a mark file in memory, which is a costly operation, adding to query latency.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyBitmapLoadMicroseconds
columns.comment: Time spent reading and deserializing UNIQUE KEY delete-bitmap sidecar files on a DeleteBitmapCache miss.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_UniqueKeyBitmapUpdates
columns.comment: Number of UNIQUE KEY delete-bitmap sidecar files written (one per supersession / DELETE commit).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PrimaryIndexCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the primary index cache, so we didn't have to load a index file.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PrimaryIndexCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the primary index cache, so we had to load a index file in memory, which is a costly operation, adding to query latency.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have not been found in the iceberg metadata cache and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheStaleMisses
columns.comment: Number of times iceberg metadata files have been found in the cache, but were considered stale and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataFilesCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the iceberg metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times paimon metadata files have been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times paimon metadata files have not been found in the paimon metadata cache and had to be read from (remote) disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PaimonMetadataFilesCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the paimon metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataReadWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time data readers spend waiting for iceberg metadata files to be read and parsed, summed across all reader threads.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times parquet metadata has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times parquet metadata has not been found in the cache and had to be read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ParquetMetadataCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the parquet metadata cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergIteratorInitializationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent on synchronous initialization of iceberg data iterators.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataUpdateMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent updating iceberg storage metadata from state (buildStorageMetadataFromState).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMetadataReturnedObjectInfos
columns.comment: Total number of returned object infos from iceberg iterator.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMinMaxNonPrunedDeleteFiles
columns.comment: Total number of accepted data files-position delete file pairs by minmax analysis from pairs suitable by partitioning and sequence number.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IcebergMinMaxPrunedDeleteFiles
columns.comment: Total number of accepted data files-position delete file pairs by minmax analysis from pairs suitable by partitioning and sequence number.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an index granule has been found in the vector index cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an index granule has not been found in the vector index cache and had to be read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_VectorSimilarityIndexCacheWeightLost
columns.comment: Approximate number of bytes evicted from the vector index cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadDictionaryBlocks
columns.comment: Number of times a text index dictionary block has been read from disk.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a text index token info has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexTokensCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a text index token info has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexHeaderCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a header has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexHeaderCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a header has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPostingsCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a text index posting list has been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPostingsCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a text index posting list has not been found in the cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadSparseIndexBlocks
columns.comment: Number of times a sparse index block has been read from the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReaderTotalMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent reading the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadGranulesMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent reading and analyzing granules of the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPositionsDecodeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent decoding text index position lists (.pos) for phrase search.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexPhraseMatchMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent in the roaringish phrase-match intersection.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexReadPostings
columns.comment: Number of times a posting list has been read from the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexUsedEmbeddedPostings
columns.comment: Number of times a posting list embedded in the dictionary has been used.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexUseHint
columns.comment: Number of index granules where a direct reading from the text index was added as hint and was used.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexDiscardHint
columns.comment: Number of index granules where a direct reading from the text index was added as hint and was discarded due to low selectivity.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyPackedBlocksDecoded
columns.comment: Number of packed blocks decoded in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyAdvanceCount
columns.comment: Number of advance operations performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsPrepared
columns.comment: Number of segments prepared (read from disk or cached) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsBuilt
columns.comment: Number of segments actually read and decoded (cache misses) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBruteForceIntersections
columns.comment: Number of brute-force intersections performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyLeapfrogIntersections
columns.comment: Number of leapfrog intersections performed in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsSkippedDense
columns.comment: Number of fully-dense segments padded as a whole (memset for OR, increment for AND) instead of decoding blocks, in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazySegmentsSkippedResolved
columns.comment: Number of segments skipped because the output region was already resolved (all-ones for OR, all-zeros for AND) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexLazyBlocksSkippedResolved
columns.comment: Number of packed blocks skipped because the output region was already resolved (all-ones for OR, all-zeros for AND) in lazy posting list mode.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexDiscardPatternScan
columns.comment: Number of times pattern-based dictionary scan in a text index was discarded because the number of posting lists to read exceeded the threshold.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexGenericExclusionSearchAlgorithm
columns.comment: Number of times the generic exclusion search algorithm is used over the text index.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_TextIndexGenericExclusionSearchStepLimitReached
columns.comment: Number of times the generic exclusion search over the text index reached merge_tree_generic_exclusion_search_max_steps and accepted the remaining mark ranges without further splitting.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryConditionCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has been found in the query condition cache (and reading of marks can be skipped). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_condition_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryConditionCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times an entry has not been found in the query condition cache (and reading of mark cannot be skipped). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_condition_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_EncryptionHeaderCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times encryption header bytes were found in the encryption header cache, so the source read of the header was skipped.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_EncryptionHeaderCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times encryption header bytes were not found in the encryption header cache, so they were read from the source.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheHits
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has been found in the query cache (and query computation was avoided). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheMisses
columns.comment: Number of times a query result has not been found in the query cache (and required query computation). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheAgeSeconds
columns.comment: The sum of ages of found query cache entries in seconds. The value is set both for hits and misses.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheReadRows
columns.comment: The number of rows read from the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheReadBytes
columns.comment: The number of (uncompressed) bytes read from the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheWrittenRows
columns.comment: The number of rows saved into the query cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryCacheWrittenBytes
columns.comment: The number of (uncompressed) bytes saved into the query cache

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferOrdinary
columns.comment: Number of times ordinary read buffer was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferDirectIO
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferDirectIOFailed
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferMMap
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer using 'mmap' was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CreatedReadBufferMMapFailed
columns.comment: Number of times a read buffer with 'mmap' was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskReadElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for read syscall. This include reads from page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskWriteElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for write syscall. This include writes to page cache.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkReceiveElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for data to receive or receiving data from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkSendElapsedMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for data to send to network or sending data to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkReceiveBytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes received from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_NetworkSendBytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes send to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_FilterPartsByVirtualColumnsMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent in filterPartsByVirtualColumns function.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolExpansions
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times new threads have been added to the global thread pool. This metric indicates the frequency of expansions in the global thread pool to accommodate increased processing demands.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolShrinks
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times the global thread pool has shrunk by removing threads. This occurs when the number of idle threads exceeds max_thread_pool_free_size, indicating adjustments in the global thread pool size in response to decreased thread utilization.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolThreadCreationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for new threads to start.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolLockWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent waiting for locks in the global thread pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolJobs
columns.comment: Counts the number of jobs that have been pushed to the global thread pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_GlobalThreadPoolJobWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Measures the elapsed time from when a job is scheduled in the thread pool to when it is picked up for execution by a worker thread. This metric helps identify delays in job processing, indicating the responsiveness of the thread pool to new tasks.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolExpansions
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times threads have been borrowed from the global thread pool to expand local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolShrinks
columns.comment: Counts the total number of times threads have been returned to the global thread pool from local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolThreadCreationMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time local thread pools have spent waiting to borrow a thread from the global pool.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolLockWaitMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent waiting for locks in the local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolJobs
columns.comment: Counts the number of jobs that have been pushed to the local thread pools.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolBusyMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time threads have spent executing the actual work.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_LocalThreadPoolJobWaitTimeMicroseconds
columns.comment: Measures the elapsed time from when a job is scheduled in the thread pool to when it is picked up for execution by a worker thread. This metric helps identify delays in job processing, indicating the responsiveness of the thread pool to new tasks.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 GET and SELECT requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of S3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of S3 GET and SELECT requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerCount
columns.comment: Number of S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests passed through throttler: blocked and not blocked.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerBlocked
columns.comment: Number of S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests blocked by throttler.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_S3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ACMEAPIRequests
columns.comment: Number of ACME API requests issued.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ACMECertificateOrders
columns.comment: Number of ACME certificate orders issued.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for Azure disk read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsCount
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read request errors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsThrottling
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read requests throttled.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureReadRequestsRedirects
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk read request redirects.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for Azure disk write requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteRequestsCount
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk write requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteRequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk write request errors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteRequestsThrottling
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk write requests throttled.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_DiskAzureWriteRequestsRedirects
columns.comment: Number of Azure disk write request redirects.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureReadMicroseconds
columns.comment: Total time spent waiting for Azure read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureReadRequestsCount
columns.comment: Number of Azure read requests.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureReadRequestsErrors
columns.comment: Number of Azure read request errors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_AzureReadRequestsThrottling

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReaderExecutorDecryptMicroseconds

columns.name: ProfileEvent_ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds
columns.comment: Modeled I/O cost of ReaderExecutor reads: a synthetic proxy KPI for read-path optimality, NOT measured latency. columns.name: ProfileEvent_CacheWarmerBytesDownloaded
columns.comment: Amount of data fetched into filesystem cache by dedicated background threads.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CacheWarmerDataPartsDownloaded
columns.comment: Number of data parts that were fully fetched by CacheWarmer.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_IgnoredColdParts
columns.comment: See setting ignore_cold_parts_seconds. Number of times read queries ignored very new parts that weren't pulled into cache by CacheWarmer yet.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PreferredWarmedUnmergedParts
columns.comment: See setting prefer_warmed_unmerged_parts_seconds. Number of times read queries used outdated pre-merge parts that are in cache instead of merged part that wasn't pulled into cache by CacheWarmer yet.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUCycles
columns.comment: Total cycles. Be wary of what happens during CPU frequency scaling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructions
columns.comment: Retired instructions. Be careful, these can be affected by various issues, most notably hardware interrupt counts.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCacheReferences
columns.comment: Cache accesses. Usually, this indicates Last Level Cache accesses, but this may vary depending on your CPU. This may include prefetches and coherency messages; again this depends on the design of your CPU.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCacheMisses
columns.comment: Cache misses. Usually this indicates Last Level Cache misses; this is intended to be used in conjunction with the PERFCOUNTHWCACHEREFERENCES event to calculate cache miss rates.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBranchInstructions
columns.comment: Retired branch instructions. Prior to Linux 2.6.35, this used the wrong event on AMD processors.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBranchMisses
columns.comment: Mispredicted branch instructions.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfBusCycles
columns.comment: Bus cycles, which can be different from total cycles.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfStalledCyclesFrontend
columns.comment: Stalled cycles during issue.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfStalledCyclesBackend
columns.comment: Stalled cycles during retirement.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfRefCPUCycles
columns.comment: Total cycles; not affected by CPU frequency scaling.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUClock
columns.comment: The CPU clock, a high-resolution per-CPU timer

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfTaskClock
columns.comment: A clock count specific to the task that is running

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfContextSwitches
columns.comment: Number of context switches

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfCPUMigrations
columns.comment: Number of times the process has migrated to a new CPU

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfAlignmentFaults
columns.comment: Number of alignment faults. These happen when unaligned memory accesses happen; the kernel can handle these but it reduces performance. This happens only on some architectures (never on x86).

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfEmulationFaults
columns.comment: Number of emulation faults. The kernel sometimes traps on unimplemented instructions and emulates them for user space. This can negatively impact performance.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfMinEnabledTime
columns.comment: For all events, minimum time that an event was enabled. Used to track event multiplexing influence

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfMinEnabledRunningTime
columns.comment: Running time for event with minimum enabled time. Used to track the amount of event multiplexing

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfDataTLBReferences

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfDataTLBMisses
columns.comment: Data TLB misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructionTLBReferences
columns.comment: Instruction TLB references

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfInstructionTLBMisses
columns.comment: Instruction TLB misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfLocalMemoryReferences
columns.comment: Local NUMA node memory reads

columns.name: ProfileEvent_PerfLocalMemoryMisses
columns.comment: Local NUMA node memory read misses

columns.name: ProfileEvent_CannotWriteToWriteBufferDiscard
columns.comment: Number of stack traces dropped by query profiler or signal handler because pipe is full or cannot write to pipe.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerSignalOverruns
columns.comment: Number of times we drop processing of a query profiler signal due to overrun plus the number of signals that OS has not delivered due to overrun.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerConcurrencyOverruns
columns.comment: Number of times we drop processing of a query profiler signal due to too many concurrent query profilers in other threads, which may indicate overload.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerRuns
columns.comment: Number of times QueryProfiler had been run.

columns.name: ProfileEvent_QueryProfilerErrors

This means that for mutations of non-replicated tables, the column will c…

Only available in ClickHouse Cloud.Note: is_killed=1 does not necessarily mean the mutation is completely finalized.It is possible for a mutation to remain in a state where is_killed=1 and is_done=0 for an extended period.This can occur if another long-running mutation is blocking the killed mutation.
