name: processes
comment: Contains a list of currently executing processes (queries) with their progress.

columns.name: is_initial_query
columns.comment: Whether this query comes directly from user or was issues by ClickHouse server in a scope of distributed query execution.

columns.name: user
columns.comment: The user who made the query. Keep in mind that for distributed processing, queries are sent to remote servers under the default user. The field contains the username for a specific query, not for a query that this query initiated.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query ID, if defined.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The IP address the query was made from. The same for distributed processing. To track where a distributed query was originally made from, look at system.processes on the query requestor server.

columns.name: port
columns.comment: The client port the query was made from.

columns.name: initial_user
columns.comment: Name of the user who ran the initial query (for distributed query execution).

columns.name: initial_query_id
columns.comment: ID of the initial query (for distributed query execution).

columns.name: initial_address
columns.comment: IP address that the parent query was launched from.

columns.name: initial_port
columns.comment: The client port that was used to make the parent query.

columns.name: interface
columns.comment: The interface which was used to send the query. TCP = 1, HTTP = 2, GRPC = 3, MYSQL = 4, POSTGRESQL = 5, LOCAL = 6, TCP_INTERSERVER = 7.

columns.name: os_user
columns.comment: Operating system username who runs clickhouse-client.

columns.name: client_hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the client machine where the clickhouse-client or another TCP client is run.

columns.name: client_name
columns.comment: The clickhouse-client or another TCP client name.

columns.name: client_agent
columns.comment: The AI coding agent that invoked the client (e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor`), detected from environment variables. Empty if no agent was detected.

columns.name: client_revision
columns.comment: Revision of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_major
columns.comment: Major version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_minor
columns.comment: Minor version of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client.

columns.name: client_version_patch
columns.comment: Patch component of the clickhouse-client or another TCP client version.

columns.name: http_method
columns.comment: HTTP method that initiated the query. Possible values: 0 — The query was launched from the TCP interface. 1 — GET method was used. 2 — POST method was used.

columns.name: http_user_agent
columns.comment: HTTP header UserAgent passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: http_referer
columns.comment: HTTP header Referer passed in the HTTP query (contains an absolute or partial address of the page making the query).

columns.name: forwarded_for
columns.comment: HTTP header X-Forwarded-For passed in the HTTP query.

columns.name: quota_key
columns.comment: The quota key specified in the quotas setting (see keyed).

columns.name: distributed_depth
columns.comment: The number of times query was retransmitted between server nodes internally.

columns.name: elapsed
columns.comment: The time in seconds since request execution started.

columns.name: is_cancelled
columns.comment: Was query cancelled.

columns.name: is_all_data_sent
columns.comment: Was all data sent to the client (in other words query had been finished on the server).

columns.name: read_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows read from the table. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: The number of uncompressed bytes read from the table. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers.

columns.name: total_rows_approx
columns.comment: The approximation of the total number of rows that should be read. For distributed processing, on the requestor server, this is the total for all remote servers. It can be updated during request processing, when new sources to process become known.

columns.name: written_rows
columns.comment: The amount of rows written to the storage.

columns.name: written_bytes
columns.comment: The amount of bytes written to the storage.

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Amount of RAM the query uses. It might not include some types of dedicated memory

columns.name: peak_memory_usage
columns.comment: The current peak of memory usage.

columns.name: query
columns.comment: The query text. For INSERT, it does not include the data to insert.

columns.name: normalized_query_hash
columns.comment: A numeric hash value, such as it is identical for queries differ only by values of literals.

columns.name: query_kind
columns.comment: The type of the query - SELECT, INSERT, etc.

columns.name: thread_ids
columns.comment: The list of identifiers of all threads which participated in this query.

columns.name: peak_threads_usage
columns.comment: Maximum count of simultaneous threads executing the query.

columns.name: ProfileEvents
columns.comment: ProfileEvents calculated for this query.

columns.name: Settings
columns.comment: The list of modified user-level settings.

columns.name: current_database
columns.comment: The name of the current database.

columns.name: is_internal
columns.comment: Indicates whether it is an auxiliary query executed internally.

name: processors_profile_log
comment: Contains profiling information on processors level (building blocks for a pipeline for query execution.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: The date when the event happened.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: The date and time when the event happened.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: The date and time with microseconds precision when the event happened.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: ID of processor.

columns.name: parent_ids
columns.comment: Parent processors IDs.

columns.name: plan_step
columns.comment: ID of the query plan step which created this processor. The value is zero if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_step_name
columns.comment: Name of the query plan step which created this processor. The value is empty if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_step_description
columns.comment: Description of the query plan step which created this processor. The value is empty if the processor was not added from any step.

columns.name: plan_group
columns.comment: Group of the processor if it was created by query plan step. A group is a logical partitioning of processors added from the same query plan step. Group is used only for beautifying the result of EXPLAIN PIPELINE result.

columns.name: initial_query_id
columns.comment: ID of the initial query (for distributed query execution).

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: ID of the query.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the processor.

columns.name: elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was executed.

columns.name: input_wait_elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was waiting for data (from other processor).

columns.name: output_wait_elapsed_us
columns.comment: Number of microseconds this processor was waiting because output port was full.

columns.name: input_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows consumed by processor.

columns.name: input_bytes
columns.comment: The number of bytes consumed by processor.

columns.name: output_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows generated by processor.

columns.name: output_bytes
columns.comment: The number of bytes generated by processor.

columns.name: processor_uniq_id
columns.comment: The uniq processor id in pipeline.

columns.name: step_uniq_id
columns.comment: The uniq step id in plan.

name: projection_parts
comment: Contains a list of currently existing projection parts (a copy of some part containing aggregated data or just sorted in different order) created for all the projections for all tables within a cluster.

columns.name: partition
columns.comment: The partition name.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the data part.

columns.name: part_type
columns.comment: The data part storing format. Possible Values: Wide (a file per column) and Compact (a single file for all columns).

columns.name: parent_name
columns.comment: The name of the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_uuid
columns.comment: The UUID of the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_part_type
columns.comment: The source (parent) data part storing format.

columns.name: active
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the data part is active. If a data part is active, it's used in a table. Otherwise, it's about to be deleted. Inactive data parts appear after merging and mutating operations.

columns.name: marks
columns.comment: The number of marks. To get the approximate number of rows in a data part, multiply marks by the index granularity (usually 8192) (this hint does not work for adaptive granularity).

columns.name: rows
columns.comment: The number of rows.

columns.name: bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the data part files in bytes.

columns.name: data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the data part. All the auxiliary files (for example, files with marks) are not included.

columns.name: marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks.

columns.name: parent_marks
columns.comment: The number of marks in the source (parent) part.

columns.name: parent_rows
columns.comment: The number of rows in the source (parent) part.

columns.name: parent_bytes_on_disk
columns.comment: Total size of all the source (parent) data part files in bytes.

columns.name: parent_data_compressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of compressed data in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_data_uncompressed_bytes
columns.comment: Total size of uncompressed data in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: parent_marks_bytes
columns.comment: The size of the file with marks in the source (parent) data part.

columns.name: modification_time
columns.comment: The time the directory with the data part was modified. This usually corresponds to the time of data part creation.

columns.name: remove_time
columns.comment: The time when the data part became inactive.

columns.name: refcount
columns.comment: The number of places where the data part is used. A value greater than 2 indicates that the data part is used in queries or merges.

columns.name: min_date
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: max_date
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date key in the data part.

columns.name: min_time
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: max_time
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key in the data part.

columns.name: partition_id
columns.comment: ID of the partition.

columns.name: min_block_number
columns.comment: The minimum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: max_block_number
columns.comment: The maximum number of data parts that make up the current part after merging.

columns.name: level
columns.comment: Depth of the merge tree. Zero means that the current part was created by insert rather than by merging other parts.

columns.name: data_version
columns.comment: Number that is used to determine which mutations should be applied to the data part (mutations with a version higher than data_version).

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) used by primary key values.

columns.name: primary_key_bytes_in_memory_allocated
columns.comment: The amount of memory (in bytes) reserved for primary key values.

columns.name: is_frozen
columns.comment: Flag that shows that a partition data backup exists. 1, the backup exists. 0, the backup does not exist.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Name of the table engine without parameters.

columns.name: disk_name
columns.comment: Name of a disk that stores the data part.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Absolute path to the folder with data part files.

columns.name: hash_of_all_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of compressed files.

columns.name: hash_of_uncompressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of uncompressed files (files with marks, index file etc.).

columns.name: uncompressed_hash_of_compressed_files
columns.comment: sipHash128 of data in the compressed files as if they were uncompressed.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: delete_ttl_info_max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the date and time key for TTL DELETE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: Array of expressions. Each expression defines a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the minimum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: move_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: Array of date and time values. Each element describes the maximum key value for a TTL MOVE rule.

columns.name: default_compression_codec
columns.comment: The name of the codec used to compress this data part (in case when there is no explicit codec for columns).

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: recompression_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: group_by_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.expression
columns.comment: The TTL expression.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.min
columns.comment: The minimum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have at least one row with expired TTL.

columns.name: rows_where_ttl_info.max
columns.comment: The maximum value of the calculated TTL expression within this part. Used to understand whether we have all rows with expired TTL.

columns.name: is_broken
columns.comment: Whether projection part is broken

columns.name: exception_code
columns.comment: Exception message explaining broken state of the projection part

columns.name: exception

columns.comment: Base directory of cache files.

columns.comment: Path of ClickHouse file, also used as metadata path.

columns.comment: Blob path in object storage, with which ClickHouse file is associated with.

columns.name: size
columns.comment: Size of the file (compressed).

columns.name: common_prefix_for_blobs
columns.comment: Common prefix for blobs in object storage.

name: replicas
comment: Contains information and status of all table replicas on current server. Each replica is represented by a single row.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: Database name.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table UUID.

columns.name: engine
columns.comment: Table engine name.

columns.name: is_leader
columns.comment: Whether the replica is the leader. Multiple replicas can be leaders at the same time. A replica can be prevented from becoming a leader using the merge_tree setting replicated_can_become_leader. The leaders are responsible for scheduling background merges. Note that writes can be performed to any replica that is available and has a session in ZK, regardless of whether it is a leader.

columns.name: can_become_leader
columns.comment: Whether the replica can be a leader.

columns.name: is_readonly
columns.comment: Whether the replica is in read-only mode. This mode is turned on if the config does not have sections with ClickHouse Keeper, if an unknown error occurred when reinitializing sessions in ClickHouse Keeper, and during session reinitialization in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: readonly_start_time
columns.comment: The timestamp when the replica transitioned into readonly mode. Null if the replica is not in readonly mode.

columns.name: is_session_expired
columns.comment: Whether the session with ClickHouse Keeper has expired. Basically the same as `is_readonly`.

columns.name: future_parts
columns.comment: The number of data parts that will appear as the result of INSERTs or merges that haven't been done yet.

columns.name: parts_to_check
columns.comment: The number of data parts in the queue for verification. A part is put in the verification queue if there is suspicion that it might be damaged.

columns.name: zookeeper_name
columns.comment: The name of the [Zoo]Keeper cluster (possibly auxiliary one) where the table's metadata is stored

columns.name: zookeeper_path
columns.comment: Path to table data in ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: replica_name
columns.comment: Replica name in ClickHouse Keeper. Different replicas of the same table have different names.

columns.name: replica_path
columns.comment: Path to replica data in ClickHouse Keeper. The same as concatenating 'zookeeper_path/replicas/replica_path'.

columns.name: columns_version
columns.comment: Version number of the table structure. Indicates how many times ALTER was performed. If replicas have different versions, it means some replicas haven't made all of the ALTERs yet.

columns.name: queue_size
columns.comment: Size of the queue for operations waiting to be performed. Operations include inserting blocks of data, merges, and certain other actions. It usually coincides with future_parts.

columns.name: inserts_in_queue
columns.comment: Number of inserts of blocks of data that need to be made. Insertions are usually replicated fairly quickly. If this number is large, it means something is wrong.

columns.name: merges_in_queue
columns.comment: The number of merges waiting to be made. Sometimes merges are lengthy, so this value may be greater than zero for a long time.

columns.name: part_mutations_in_queue
columns.comment: The number of mutations waiting to be made.

columns.name: queue_oldest_time
columns.comment: If `queue_size` greater than 0, shows when the oldest operation was added to the queue.

columns.name: inserts_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: merges_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: part_mutations_oldest_time
columns.comment: See `queue_oldest_time`.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_get
columns.comment: The name of the part to fetch from other replicas obtained from the oldest GET_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_merge_to
columns.comment: The result part name to merge to obtained from the oldest MERGE_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: oldest_part_to_mutate_to
columns.comment: The result part name to mutate to obtained from the oldest MUTATE_PARTS entry in the replication queue.

columns.name: log_max_index
columns.comment: Maximum entry number in the log of general activity. This column and the next three (`log_pointer`, `total_replicas`, `active_replicas`) have a non-zero value only where there is an active session with ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: log_pointer
columns.comment: Maximum entry number in the log of general activity that the replica copied to its execution queue, plus one. If log_pointer is much smaller than log_max_index, something is wrong.

columns.name: last_queue_update
columns.comment: When the queue was updated last time.

columns.name: absolute_delay
columns.comment: How big lag in seconds the current replica has.

columns.name: total_replicas
columns.comment: The total number of known replicas of this table.

columns.name: active_replicas
columns.comment: The number of replicas of this table that have a session in ClickHouse Keeper (i.e., the number of functioning replicas).

columns.name: lost_part_count
columns.comment: The number of data parts lost in the table by all replicas in total since table creation. Value is persisted in ClickHouse Keeper and can only increase.

columns.name: last_queue_update_exception
columns.comment: When the queue contains broken entries. Especially important when ClickHouse breaks backward compatibility between versions and log entries written by newer versions aren't parseable by old versions.

columns.name: zookeeper_exception
columns.comment: The last exception message, got if the error happened when fetching the info from ClickHouse Keeper.

columns.name: replica_is_active
columns.comment: Map between replica name and is replica active.

columns.comment: Name of the database.

columns.name: table
columns.comment: Name of the table.

columns.name: elapsed
columns.comment: The time elapsed (in seconds) since showing currently running background fetches started.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: The percentage of completed work from 0 to 1.

columns.name: result_part_name

columns.name: lifetime_rows
columns.comment: Total number of rows INSERTed since server start (only for Buffer tables).

columns.name: lifetime_bytes
columns.comment: Total number of bytes INSERTed since server start (only for Buffer tables).

columns.name: comment
columns.comment: The comment for the table.

columns.name: has_own_data
columns.comment: Flag that indicates whether the table itself stores some data on disk or only accesses some other source.

columns.name: loading_dependencies_database
columns.comment: Database loading dependencies (list of objects which should be loaded before the current object).

columns.name: loading_dependencies_table
columns.comment: Table loading dependencies (list of objects which should be loaded before the current object).

columns.name: loading_dependent_database
columns.comment: Dependent loading database.

columns.name: loading_dependent_table
columns.comment: Dependent loading table.

columns.name: target_database
columns.comment: For a materialized view, the database of the destination table the view writes to (the `TO` target, or the implicit `.inner.*` table). Empty for other engines.

columns.name: target_table
columns.comment: For a materialized view, the name of the destination table the view writes to (the `TO` target, or the implicit `.inner.*` table). Empty for other engines.

columns.name: definer
columns.comment: SQL security definer's name used for the table.

name: text_log
comment: Contains logging entries which are normally written to a log file or to stdout.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Date of the entry.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Time of the entry.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Time of the entry with microseconds precision.

columns.name: thread_name
columns.comment: Name of the thread from which the logging was done.

columns.name: thread_id
columns.comment: OS thread ID.

columns.name: level
columns.comment: Entry level. Possible values: 1 or 'Fatal', 2 or 'Critical', 3 or 'Error', 4 or 'Warning', 5 or 'Notice', 6 or 'Information', 7 or 'Debug', 8 or 'Trace'.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: ID of the query.

columns.name: logger_name
columns.comment: Name of the logger (e.g., DDLWorker).

columns.name: message
columns.comment: The message itself.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: ClickHouse revision.

columns.name: source_file
columns.comment: Source file from which the logging was done.

columns.name: source_line
columns.comment: Source line from which the logging was done.

columns.name: message_format_string
columns.comment: A format string that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value1
columns.comment: Argument 1 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value2
columns.comment: Argument 2 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value3
columns.comment: Argument 3 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value4
columns.comment: Argument 4 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value5
columns.comment: Argument 5 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value6
columns.comment: Argument 6 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value7
columns.comment: Argument 7 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value8
columns.comment: Argument 8 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value9
columns.comment: Argument 9 that was used to format the message.

columns.name: value10
columns.comment: Argument 10 that was used to format the message.

name: time_zones
comment: Contains a list of time zones that are supported by the ClickHouse server. This list of timezones might vary depending on the version of ClickHouse.

columns.name: time_zone
columns.comment: List of supported time zones.

name: tokenizers
comment: Contains a list of the available tokenizers.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Name of the tokenizer

name: trace_log
comment: Contains stack traces collected by the sampling query profiler.

columns.name: hostname
columns.comment: Hostname of the server executing the query.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Date of sampling moment.

columns.name: event_time
columns.comment: Timestamp of the sampling moment.

columns.name: event_time_microseconds
columns.comment: Timestamp of the sampling moment with microseconds precision.

columns.name: timestamp_ns
columns.comment: Timestamp of the sampling moment in nanoseconds.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: ClickHouse server build revision. When connecting to the server by `clickhouse-client`, you see a string similar to `Connected to ClickHouse server version 19.18.1.`. This field contains the `revision`, but not the `version` of a server.

columns.name: trace_type
columns.comment: Trace type: `Real` represents collecting stack traces by wall-clock time. `CPU` represents collecting stack traces by CPU time. `Memory` represents collecting allocations and deallocations when memory allocation exceeds the subsequent watermark. `MemorySample` represents collecting random allocations and deallocations. `MemoryPeak` represents collecting updates of peak memory usage. `ProfileEve…

columns.name: cpu_id
columns.comment: CPU identifier.

columns.name: thread_id
columns.comment: Thread identifier.

columns.name: thread_name
columns.comment: Thread name.

columns.name: query_id
columns.comment: Query identifier that can be used to get details about a query that was running from the query_log system table.

columns.name: trace
columns.comment: Stack trace at the moment of sampling. Each element is a virtual memory address inside ClickHouse server process.

columns.name: size
columns.comment: For trace types Memory, MemorySample, MemoryAllocatedWithoutCheck or MemoryPeak is the amount of memory allocated, for other trace types is 0.

columns.name: ptr
columns.comment: The address of the allocated chunk.

columns.name: memory_context
columns.comment: Memory Tracker context (only for Memory/MemoryPeak): `Unknown` context is not defined for this trace_type. `Global` represents server context. `User` represents user/merge context. `Process` represents process (i.e. query) context. `Thread` represents thread (thread of particular process) context. `Max` this is a special value means that memory tracker is not blocked (for blocked_context column).

columns.name: memory_blocked_context
columns.comment: Context for which memory tracker is blocked (for ClickHouse developers only): `Unknown` context is not defined for this trace_type. `Global` represents server context. `User` represents user/merge context. `Process` represents process (i.e. query) context. `Thread` represents thread (thread of particular process) context. `Max` this is a special value means that memory tracker is not blocked (f…

columns.name: event
columns.comment: For trace type ProfileEvent is the name of updated profile event, for other trace types is an empty string.

columns.name: increment
columns.comment: For trace type ProfileEvent is the amount of increment of profile event, for other trace types is 0.

columns.name: symbols
columns.comment: If the symbolization is enabled, contains demangled symbol names, corresponding to the `trace`. Symbolization can be enabled or disabled in the `symbolize` setting under `trace_log` in the server configuration file.

columns.name: lines
columns.comment: If the symbolization is enabled, contains strings with file names with line numbers, corresponding to the `trace`.

columns.name: function_id
columns.comment: For trace type Instrumentation, ID assigned to the function in xray_instr_map section of elf-binary.

columns.name: function_name
columns.comment: For trace type Instrumentation, name of the instrumented function.

columns.name: handler
columns.comment: For trace type Instrumentation, handler of the instrumented function.

columns.name: entry_type
columns.comment: For trace type Instrumentation, entry type of the instrumented function.

columns.name: duration_nanoseconds
columns.comment: For trace type Instrumentation, time the function was running for in nanoseconds.

name: unicode
comment: Contains all unicode codepoints.

columns.name: code_point
columns.comment: The Unicode code point represented as U+XXXX.

columns.name: code_point_value
columns.comment: The integer value of the Unicode code point.

columns.name: notation
columns.comment: The character notation (visual representation of the code point).

name: user_defined_functions
comment: Shows all user-defined executable functions with their metadata, configuration, and loading status.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: UDF name.

columns.name: load_status
columns.comment: Loading status. Possible values: Success — UDF loaded and ready to use, Failed — UDF failed to load (see field 'loading_error_message' for details).

columns.name: loading_error_message
columns.comment: Detailed error message when loading failed. Empty if loaded successfully.

columns.name: last_successful_update_time
columns.comment: Timestamp of the last successful update. NULL if never succeeded.

columns.name: loading_duration_ms
columns.comment: Time spent loading the UDF, in milliseconds.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: UDF type: 'executable' (single process) or 'executable_pool' (process pool).

columns.name: command
columns.comment: Script or command to execute for this UDF.

columns.name: format
columns.comment: Data format for I/O (e.g., 'TabSeparated', 'JSONEachRow').

columns.name: return_type
columns.comment: Function return type (e.g., 'String', 'UInt64').

columns.name: return_name
columns.comment: Optional return value identifier. Empty if not configured.

columns.name: argument_types
columns.comment: Array of argument types (e.g., ['String', 'UInt64']).

columns.name: argument_names
columns.comment: Array of argument names. Empty strings for unnamed arguments.

columns.name: max_command_execution_time
columns.comment: Maximum seconds to process a data block. Only for 'executable_pool' type.

columns.name: command_termination_timeout
columns.comment: Seconds before sending SIGTERM to command process.

columns.name: command_read_timeout
columns.comment: Milliseconds for reading from command stdout.

columns.name: command_write_timeout
columns.comment: Milliseconds for writing to command stdin.

columns.name: pool_size
columns.comment: Number of command process instances. Only for 'executable_pool' type.

columns.name: send_chunk_header
columns.comment: Whether to send row count before each data chunk (boolean).

columns.name: execute_direct
columns.comment: Whether to execute command directly (1) or via /bin/bash (0).

columns.name: lifetime
columns.comment: Reload interval in seconds. 0 means reload is disabled.

columns.name: deterministic
columns.comment: Whether function returns the same result for the same arguments (boolean).

name: user_directories
comment: Contains the information about configured user directories - directories on the file system from which ClickHouse server is allowed to read user provided data.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the directory.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The type of the access storage e.g. users.xml or replicated or memory etc.

columns.name: params
columns.comment: JSON with the parameters of the access storage.

columns.name: precedence
columns.comment: The order in which this directory is declared in the config. The same order is used when ClickHouse tries to find a user or role.

name: user_processes
comment: This system table can be used to get overview of memory usage and ProfileEvents of users.

columns.name: user
columns.comment: User name.

columns.name: memory_usage
columns.comment: Sum of RAM used by all processes of the user. It might not include some types of dedicated memory. See the max_memory_usage setting.

columns.name: peak_memory_usage
columns.comment: The peak of memory usage of the user. It can be reset when no queries are run for the user.

columns.name: ProfileEvents
columns.comment: Summary of ProfileEvents that measure different metrics for the user. The description of them could be found in the table system.events

name: users
comment: Contains a list of all users profiles either configured at the server through a configuration file or created via SQL.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: User name.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: User ID.

columns.name: storage
columns.comment: Path to the storage of users. Configured in the access_control_path parameter.

columns.name: auth_type
columns.comment: Shows the authentication types. There are multiple ways of user identification: with no password, with plain text password, with SHA256-encoded password, with double SHA-1-encoded password or with bcrypt-encoded password.

columns.name: auth_params
columns.comment: Authentication parameters in the JSON format depending on the auth_type.

columns.name: valid_until
columns.comment: The expiration date and time for user credentials.

columns.name: host_ip
columns.comment: IP addresses of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names
columns.comment: Names of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names_regexp
columns.comment: Regular expression for host names that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server.

columns.name: host_names_like
columns.comment: Names of hosts that are allowed to connect to the ClickHouse server, set using the LIKE predicate.

columns.name: default_roles_all
columns.comment: Shows that all granted roles set for user by default.

columns.name: default_roles_list
columns.comment: List of granted roles provided by default.

columns.name: default_roles_except
columns.comment: All the granted roles set as default excepting of the listed ones.

columns.name: grantees_any
columns.comment: The flag that indicates whether a user with any grant option can grant it to anyone.

columns.name: grantees_list
columns.comment: The list of users or roles to which this user is allowed to grant options to.

columns.name: grantees_except
columns.comment: The list of users or roles to which this user is forbidden from grant options to.

columns.name: default_database
columns.comment: The name of the default database for this user.

name: view_refreshes
comment: Lists all Refreshable Materialized Views of current server.

columns.name: database
columns.comment: The name of the database the table is in.

columns.name: view
columns.comment: Table name.

columns.name: uuid
columns.comment: Table uuid (Atomic database).

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Current state of the refresh.

columns.name: last_success_time
columns.comment: Time when the latest successful refresh started. NULL if no successful refreshes happened since server startup or table creation.

columns.name: last_success_duration_ms
columns.comment: How long the latest refresh took.

columns.name: last_refresh_time
columns.comment: Time when the latest refresh attempt finished (if known) or started (if unknown or still running). NULL if no refresh attempts happened since server startup or table creation.

columns.name: last_refresh_replica
columns.comment: If coordination is enabled, name of the replica that made the current (if running) or previous (if not running) refresh attempt.

columns.name: next_refresh_time
columns.comment: Time at which the next refresh is scheduled to start. NULL if the next refresh time is not currently known, e.g. when waiting for dependencies (status `WaitingForDependencies` or `MissingDependencies`).

columns.name: exception
columns.comment: Error message from previous attempt if it failed.

columns.name: retry
columns.comment: How many failed attempts there were so far, for the current refresh. Not available if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: Progress of the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica, between 0 and 1. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica` or the refresh is not running.

columns.name: read_rows
columns.comment: Number of rows read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`.

columns.name: read_bytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: total_rows
columns.comment: Estimated total number of rows that need to be read by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: written_rows
columns.comment: Number of rows written by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

columns.name: written_bytes
columns.comment: Number of bytes written by the current running or most recently completed refresh at the given replica. NULL if status is `RunningOnAnotherReplica`

name: warnings
comment: Contains warnings about server configuration to be displayed by clickhouse-client right after it connects to the server.

columns.name: message
columns.comment: A warning message issued by ClickHouse server.

columns.name: message_format_string
columns.comment: A format string that was used to format the message.

name: workloads
comment: Contains a list of all currently existing workloads.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The name of the workload.

columns.name: parent
columns.comment: The name of the parent workload.

columns.name: create_query
columns.comment: CREATE query of the workload.

name: zeros
comment: Produces unlimited number of non-materialized zeros.

columns.name: zero
columns.comment: dummy

name: zeros_mt
comment: Multithreaded version of system.zeros.

columns.comment: dummy
